clue.text: Ideas involved with Nick N may be this?

definitions.text: Ideas involved with Nick N may be this?

indicators.note: involved means tangled up or intricate, so these letters are jumbled together

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A suggestion that plots tangled around a character called Nick N would suit a Victorian novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange IDEAS, NICK and N; the result describes something in the manner of the Victorian novelist, the kind of tale whose plots are 'involved' — so the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens was famed for convoluted plots and odd character names, so involved ideas around a named Nick are characteristic of his style.

clue.text: Part of organ sinks back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for sinks from right to left

parts.note: to sink a ball in snooker is to pot it, so sinks is pots

explanation.surface: A piece of a church organ subsides backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns POTS around. 'Part of organ' could suggest a body organ, but here it is the knob on a pipe organ selecting a set of pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: On a pipe organ a stop is the control, or set of pipes, it brings into play.

clue.text: Chemist no longer having hesitation about uranium

parts.note: something no longer current is past

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the hesitation sound goes around the chemical symbol

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A chemist who has stopped dithering over uranium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets the hesitation sound around the uranium symbol. Louis Pasteur, the French chemist, gave his name to pasteurisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was a famous French chemist and microbiologist, so he is an example of a chemist.

clue.text: Surgeon's principal vocation will involve exercises — with this?

definitions.text: Surgeon's principal vocation will involve exercises — with this?

indicators.note: principal means leading or first, so take the opening letter of the word
involve means take in, so the word for vocation encloses the exercises

parts.note: a vocation is a calling, or call
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: A surgeon's main work involves exercises — and an instrument to do them with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will involve' sets the exercises inside the vocation word. Read as a whole, the clue describes the surgeon's working blade, so it is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalpel is the small sharp knife a surgeon operates with, the tool of the surgical calling.

clue.text: Difficulty in sight? English agreed to prepare

parts.note: yes is the word of agreement
to train is to prepare someone for something

explanation.surface: An English team agrees to get ready, though a problem looms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Difficulty in sight' reads as trouble ahead, but means a strain on the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiredness or discomfort of the eyes from overuse is a difficulty with one's vision.

clue.text: I sort out wool prior…to producing this?

definitions.text: I sort out wool prior…to producing this?

indicators.note: prior means before, so the carding word is placed ahead of the letter I

parts.note: to card wool is to comb out its fibres before spinning

explanation.surface: Someone combing wool in advance of knitting a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prior' puts CARD before I. Carding wool is a step towards knitting the woolly garment, so the clue as a whole defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardi, short for cardigan, is a knitted woollen jacket, the end product of processing wool.

clue.text: Nothing to be added to concert advertisement

indicators.note: added to means joined on after, so nothing is placed at the end of the concert

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms
O is the zero shape, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing more needs adding to the concert publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be added to' places O after PROM. The Proms are a famous series of London summer concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: A promo is a short promotional piece, so it is an informal word for an advertisement.

clue.text: Clumsy fellow coming in to damage love and sexual attraction

indicators.note: coming in to means entering, so the fellow goes inside the word for damage

parts.note: to mar is to damage
a lad is a young fellow
love is nil in tennis, the letter O
it is an old term for sex appeal

explanation.surface: An awkward chap barges in and spoils romance and allure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in to' sets the fellow inside the damage word. 'Clumsy fellow' looks like the definition, but 'fellow' is the inserted piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladroit means lacking skill or dexterity, which is to say clumsy or awkward.

clue.text: Inept duel mishandled in entirety

indicators.note: mishandled means badly managed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A badly fought duel, botched from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mishandled' rearranges INEPT and DUEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenitude means fullness or completeness, the state of being whole, which is entirety.

clue.text: Soldiers to stop you retreating — from me?

definitions.text: Soldiers to stop you retreating — from me?

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the assembled letters are read from right to left
to stop means to plug a gap, so the soldiers go inside the word for you

parts.note: ye is an old word for you
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Troops sent to block your escape — perhaps by me?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stop' plugs the soldiers inside the old word for you, giving YMENE, and 'retreating' turns that round. Soldiers sent to stop you are your foe, so the clue as a whole defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sends soldiers against you is your adversary or foe.

clue.text: Domain almost entirely encountered in sleep pattern?

indicators.note: encountered in means found inside, so the trimmed word sits within the sleep phase

parts.note: REM is rapid eye movement, a phase of sleep

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: entirely means all, wholly

explanation.surface: A whole territory glimpsed in a dream state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the word for entirely, and 'encountered in' sets the result inside the sleep phase. REM sleep is when we dream.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom or field of activity, which is a domain.

clue.text: Knight captured by peasants — wrongly — in this move?

indicators.note: captured by means held inside, so the chess knight goes into the reshuffled letters
wrongly means incorrectly arranged, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight taken by pawns — peasants — in an improper chess play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges PEASANTS to EPASSANT, and 'captured by' puts N in it. The chess theme of knights, peasants (pawns) and capture is the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: En passant is a special chess move in which a pawn captures an enemy pawn that has just advanced two squares.

clue.text: Opera composer has openings for contralto and tenor in conclusion

parts.note: Verdi was the Italian opera composer of Aida and La Traviata

indicators.note: openings are the first letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: An opera composer gives contralto and tenor their starts in the finale.
explanation.walkthrough: VERDI, then C and T from the first letters of 'contralto' and 'tenor'. The musical surface hides a courtroom sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A verdict is a finding or judgement reached at the end of a case, a conclusion.

clue.text: Bar abandoning new idea gets enthusiastic response

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so the bar is taken out of the new idea

parts.note: an innovation is a new idea or method
an inn is a pub or bar

explanation.surface: A notion of quitting the pub draws wild applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' removes INN from the front of INNOVATION.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovation is a burst of applause from an audience, an enthusiastic reception.

clue.text: List source of abusive comments, perhaps, omitting first one

indicators.note: omitting the first one means dropping the opening letter of the word

parts.note: an internet troll posts abusive comments, an example of such a source

explanation.surface: A list of where nasty remarks come from, leaving out the first culprit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'omitting first one' removes the T from TROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll is an official list of names, as in an electoral roll or roll call.

clue.text: Chapter One: note singular skill keeping millions enthralled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the skill word holds the abbreviation for millions

parts.note: talent is skill or ability

explanation.surface: A book's opening chapter reveals a rare gift that captivates millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts M inside TALENT to give TALMENT, after I, N and S. 'Chapter One' reads as a heading but splits into definition and I; 'enthralled' only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An instalment is one part of a story published in sequence, like a chapter of a serial.

clue.text: Line cutting mug in two

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the line goes inside the word for mug

parts.note: a mug is a gullible person, a dupe

explanation.surface: A line slicing a cup into two halves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' puts L inside DUPE. 'mug' looks like a cup but is a sucker.
explanation.definitionFit: Duple describes musical time with two beats to the bar, so it means in two.

clue.text: Meat dish, turkey, brought into church function

indicators.note: brought into means placed inside, so the fool goes within the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a turkey is a fool or flop, an ass
a role is a function or job

explanation.surface: A turkey dish served at a church dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought into' sets the fool inside the church letters. 'turkey' looks like the meat for the dish, but it means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A casserole is a slow-cooked stew of meat in a covered dish.

clue.text: Complex cinematic role with large message on screen?

indicators.note: complex means intricate or tangled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An elaborate film part with a big communication on the cinema screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' rearranges CINEMATIC and ROLE to ELECTRONICMAI, then L. 'screen' suggests cinema, but here it is a computer monitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Email is a message sent and read on a computer screen.

clue.text: Scornful attitude reduced money invested in Mars shot

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, so the shortened money goes into the scrambled planet name
shot means ruined or wrecked, so these letters are rearranged
reduced means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: cash is money

explanation.surface: Withering contempt after cuts to funds for a Mars mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' scrambles the planet name to SARM, 'reduced' trims the money word, and 'invested in' sets it inside SARM.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcasm is mocking, cutting irony expressing contempt, a scornful attitude.

clue.text: Stadium left to accommodate second soccer team

indicators.note: accommodate means house or take in, so the stadium holds the abbreviation for second

parts.note: an arena is a stadium

explanation.surface: A ground left to house a second football side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accommodate' puts S inside ARENA to give ARSENA, then L. Arsenal is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a famous professional football club from north London, an example of a soccer team.

clue.text: Try to get money from old taxmen for animal

parts.note: to tap someone is to ask them for money
IR is the Inland Revenue, the former UK tax authority

explanation.surface: Trying to squeeze cash out of former tax inspectors on behalf of a creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inland Revenue was the UK tax office before it merged into HMRC in 2005.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapir is a hoofed mammal of the tropics with a short flexible snout, so it is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Associate vague about source of rough forecasting methodology

parts.note: a pal is a friend or associate

indicators.note: about means around, so the hazy word surrounds the letter taken from rough

parts.note: misty means hazy or vague

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A friend is hazy about where a rough prediction comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' takes the first letter of 'rough', and 'about' wraps the hazy word around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Palmistry claims to tell a person's future from the lines of the hand, a method of forecasting.

clue.text: A celebration of irregular habits

parts.note: habits are worn clothes, not behaviour, so this is a party where guests wear unusual costumes

explanation.surface: A party in honour of odd behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habits' suggests routines, but it means garments, as a monk's habit; 'irregular' means out of the ordinary costume.
explanation.definitionFit: A party where guests come dressed in costumes is a festive event celebrating unusual outfits.

clue.text: Pretend there's no real problem with being through with The Times?

parts.note: The Times is a newspaper, a paper
being through means finished, over

explanation.surface: Ignoring a problem because one has finished reading The Times.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue nods to its own newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To paper over a problem is to conceal it, pretending it does not exist.

clue.text: Functioning musical taken up after music-drama falling short

indicators.note: after places the musical behind the shortened music-drama
falling short means not reaching the end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an opera is a drama set to music

indicators.note: in a down clue taken up means lifted, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.surface: A stage musical revived following an opera that underperformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling short' trims the music-drama; 'taken up' turns the musical into ATIVE, which 'after' puts behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Operative means in effect or working, which is functioning.

clue.text: Not out, not bowled, not taken in

indicators.note: not here means without, so the cricket letter for bowled is removed

parts.note: in cricket a batsman not out is unbeaten
B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A list of cricket scorecard terms: not out, not bowled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes B from UNBEATEN. In cricket a batter who is 'not out' at the end of an innings is unbeaten; 'not taken in' means not swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is uneaten has not been consumed, or taken into the body.

clue.text: Achievement? Retired airman having one further back

parts.note: ex means former, retired

indicators.note: further back means moved towards the end, so the letter for one shifts later in the word

parts.note: a pilot is an airman
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Is it an achievement when a retired flyer has one more pushed to the rear?
explanation.walkthrough: 'further back' shifts the one in the airman word later, giving PLOIT. An exploit is a feat, hence the question mark on a slightly loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploit is a bold or daring deed, an achievement.

clue.text: Feel bad about parking on right for thirty days

indicators.note: about means around, so the ailing word surrounds the two abbreviations

parts.note: to ail is to feel ill

indicators.note: in a down clue on means above, so parking sits over right

explanation.surface: Feeling unwell over parking on the right for a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts PR inside AIL. 'on' is a down-clue convention: P is placed above R.
explanation.definitionFit: April is a month with thirty days, so it is defined by its length.

clue.text: Some canvassing to secure European opinion

indicators.note: secure means hold fast, so the tent encloses the abbreviation for European

parts.note: a tent is made of canvas, some canvassing

explanation.surface: A bit of electioneering to win a European's view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canvassing' looks like seeking votes, but means canvas material, a tent. 'to secure' puts E inside TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief held, which is an opinion.
